stack.summary: The fixture is a private ESM Node service using TypeScript and a small JavaScript adapter surface, with TSX/JSX UI files. package.json runs Node's experimental strip-types test command; tsconfig targets ES2022/NodeNext with strict checking, allowJs, JSX preserve, and noEmit.

sections.heading: Languages and runtime
sections.content: The source combines TypeScript domain, application, HTTP, persistence and contract modules with JavaScript request/response and adapter helpers plus TSX/JSX UI components. Runtime code uses Node built-ins; the UUID adapter imports node:crypto.

sections.heading: Configuration
sections.content: loadConfig supplies PORT=8080 and RESERVATION_HORIZON_DAYS=7 defaults, then rejects non-integer or out-of-range values (ports 1-65535; horizon 1-30 days).

architecture.summary: Requests flow from routeRequest through reservation-routes and the ReservationService into domain validation and repository lookups, then return JSON responses. createService composes the service with in-memory repositories, a system clock and UUID-backed IDs.

sections.heading: Request flow
sections.content: POST /reservations validates a body before calling service.create; GET /reservations/:id reads a view; POST /reservations/:id/confirm and /cancel apply state transitions. Unknown reservation paths return route_not_found through the router.

sections.heading: Layer boundaries
sections.content: ReservationService owns orchestration and dependency injection. Reservation, Member, Tool and reservation-policy enforce domain behavior; repository interfaces abstract lookups/saves while the current server wiring selects in-memory implementations.

structure.summary: The tree is organized by domain, application, contracts, HTTP, persistence, adapters, types and UI under src, with focused node:test files under tests. Reservation behavior is represented by a domain aggregate and a service over repository ports.

sections.heading: Source areas
sections.content: src/domain defines Member, Tool, Reservation and errors; src/application contains ReservationService; src/persistence contains repository interfaces and in-memory adapters; src/http contains parsing, route handling and response translation; src/contracts and src/types define transport and branded-ID shapes.

sections.heading: Entrypoints and UI
sections.content: src/server.ts exposes createService, createDemoService and routeRequest. reservation-form.tsx posts a tool reservation form, while reservation-summary.jsx renders a status label and time range.

conventions.summary: Typed modules use exported type aliases, interfaces, classes and functions with explicit readonly state where appropriate. IDs are branded string types, domain transitions return new Reservation values, and JavaScript helpers remain small named ESM functions.

sections.heading: Types and state
sections.content: MemberId, ToolId and ReservationId are branded strings with as*Id constructors. Domain entities expose readonly fields; Reservation keeps private parts and uses confirm/cancel to create updated values rather than mutating its status.

sections.heading: Validation and naming
sections.content: Constructors and factories throw typed DomainError subclasses for invalid state; policy errors use ConflictError, missing resources use NotFoundError, and HTTP validation uses ValidationError. Names follow descriptive PascalCase classes and camelCase functions.

testing.summary: The fixture uses node:test with three focused suites for configuration, application behavior and routing. Tests cover creation, confirmation, overlap rejection, cancellation reuse, HTTP status/body translation, malformed request bodies and unknown paths; README also documents a no-listener test baseline and a strict TypeScript noEmit check.

sections.heading: Application cases
sections.content: reservation-service.test.ts fixes the clock and ID sequence, then verifies held-to-confirmed transitions, overlapping tool rejection and cancellation releasing a time window.

sections.heading: HTTP and configuration cases
sections.content: router.test.ts exercises POST/GET/confirm routes, stable 404 and 400 JSON errors, unknown nested paths and /health; config.test.ts checks defaults and invalid PORT rejection.

integrations.summary: The runtime integration surface is intentionally local: HTTP-shaped request/response records feed the router, repositories provide member/tool/reservation access, and adapters supply a system clock and random UUID IDs. The UI form posts to /reservations and the summary consumes ReservationView-like status and timestamps.

sections.heading: Injected ports
sections.content: ReservationService receives MemberRepository, ToolRepository, ReservationRepository, now and nextId dependencies. The server binds the three in-memory repositories, systemClock and newReservationId; no external package or network client is used by the fixture runtime.

sections.heading: Presentation boundary
sections.content: HTTP responses carry application/json bodies. reservation-form.tsx submits startsAt and endsAt fields with a tool data attribute, while reservation-summary.jsx displays Cancelled or Reserved from reservation.status.

concerns.summary: The prepared map contains 34 files: 14 with full parsed coverage, 15 TypeScript source/test files with file-level partial coverage, and 5 unsupported-language records for SQL, configuration or documentation. Runtime persistence is in-memory and tests call the router directly; the role of reservations.sql is not established by executable source.

sections.heading: Evidence limits
sections.content: The preparation reports unsupported-construct partial coverage for server.ts, reservation-routes.ts, config.ts, repository ports/adapters, branded IDs and all three test files. It reports unsupported-language file coverage for reservations.sql, package.json, tsconfig.json, README.md and AGENTS.md, so semantic details from those records are limited to file-level evidence.

sections.heading: Runtime scope
sections.content: The observed executable composition creates in-memory repositories and does not start a network listener. The SQL file is present but its runtime integration is unknown from the prepared source; durable persistence, deployment and production readiness are outside this fixture's evidence.

capabilities.name: Reserve a tool window
capabilities.summary: Creates a held reservation after member and tool lookup, timestamp validation, reservation policy checks and repository save.

capabilities.name: Manage reservation lifecycle
capabilities.summary: Reads reservations and applies confirm or cancel transitions, returning the resulting ReservationView.

capabilities.name: Enforce reservation policy
capabilities.summary: Allows only active members and ready tools, caps open member reservations at three, and rejects overlapping non-cancelled tool reservations.

capabilities.name: Expose reservation HTTP API
capabilities.summary: Handles create, get, confirm and cancel reservation routes with validated request bodies and JSON responses.

capabilities.name: Translate domain errors
capabilities.summary: Maps DomainError codes to stable HTTP statuses and JSON error bodies while preserving a 404 route_not_found response for unmatched routes.

capabilities.name: Compose in-memory service
capabilities.summary: Builds ReservationService with in-memory member, tool and reservation repositories, the system clock, and random UUID reservation IDs.

capabilities.name: Validate service configuration
capabilities.summary: Loads bounded PORT and reservation-horizon settings from environment values with safe defaults and typed validation errors.

capabilities.name: Render reservation UI
capabilities.summary: Provides a tool reservation form with datetime fields and a status summary that displays reservation state and time range.

claims.statement: ReservationService.create looks up the member and tool, parses date strings, constructs a Reservation, applies policy, saves it and returns its view.
Reservation.create rejects invalid timestamps, non-positive windows, past starts and durations outside two hours through seven days; new reservations default to held.
assertReservationAllowed rejects suspended members, non-ready tools, members with three or more open reservations, and any supplied conflicting reservation.
Reservation.overlaps ignores cancelled reservations and uses strict interval comparisons, so a cancelled booking releases the interval and touching endpoints do not overlap.
InMemoryReservationRepository stores reservations by branded ID and finds by ID, member, or overlapping tool window.
ReservationService.get returns a view or throws NotFoundError; confirm changes held to confirmed, while cancel is idempotent for cancelled reservations.
The HTTP boundary serves POST /reservations, GET /reservations/:id, and POST /reservations/:id/confirm or /cancel with status 201 or 200 on success.
Create requests require non-empty memberId, toolId, startsAt and endsAt strings before service invocation.
routeRequest maps not_found to 404, conflict to 409, other DomainError values to 400, unexpected errors to 500, and unmatched routes to a 404 route_not_found JSON body.
createService wires in-memory repositories, systemClock and newReservationId; createDemoService seeds one member and one ready cordless drill.
loadConfig defaults port to 8080 and reservationHorizonDays to 7, then validates the configured numeric ranges.
ReservationForm posts to /reservations with required datetime-local startsAt and endsAt fields, while ReservationSummary labels cancelled records Cancelled and all other states Reserved.

ReservationService can receive alternate member, tool and reservation storage implementations because its dependency type names repository interfaces and the server separately chooses in-memory implementations.
The prepared inventory includes src/persistence/reservations.sql, but its runtime role and whether it is used are unknown from the executable source evidence.
